Employment Potential
The construction and labor force requirements for the various levels of Westmoreland production are shown in Table III-2. The degree and extent of the socio-economic impact associated with Westmoreland's development will be in direct relationship to the kind and amount of employment generated. These include both direct employment in the mine and the very considerable induced employment resulting from added economic activity created by these developments.
The several possible eventual levels of coal development have already been described in detail. Table III-2 provides a summary of employment for each of these during the construction and production (operations) phases.
Implications of Crow Indian Labor Force Participation Rates
The population, labor force, and employment implications of proposed mining by Westmoreland Resources differ substantially depending upon which of the two labor force participation rates and depending upon which of the two alternative futures is assumed. A principal determinant of the size of the non-Crow population of the impact area will be the way in which the Crows choose to participate in the labor force. If Crow participation rates increase, local employment needs will be better met locally, and there will be less non-Crow in-migration. Under these circumstances Crows will become a larger proportion of the impact area population and will have a larger proportion of the jobs. A lower Crow labor force participation rate, would require a larger non-Crow population in order to satisfy any given basic employment requirements.
